subject.title: [Feature]: Memory durability config — hard flush threshold, priority-aware compaction, cache TTL

question: Should OpenClaw add public config/runtime contracts for hard token memory flush, priority-preserving compaction metadata, and embedding-cache TTL, and which parts should be accepted or rejected?
rationale: The current code lacks all three requested keys, but adding them changes public memory/config semantics and partly overlaps existing compaction lifecycle, memory plugin, and content-hash cache behavior.

options.title: Split And Decide Each Contract
options.body: Approve, reject, or redesign hard flush, priority preservation, and TTL independently before implementation so the public config surface stays narrow.

options.title: Accept Bundled Durability Package
options.body: Treat the three knobs as one production-memory durability package and require fresh-install, upgrade, and scale proof before merge.

options.title: Defer New Config Surface
options.body: Keep current memory flush/search behavior and route remaining cache and priority work to narrower existing or future issues unless maintainers explicitly accept new config.

recommendation.title: Split And Decide Each Contract
recommendation.body: Approve, reject, or redesign hard flush, priority preservation, and TTL independently before implementation so the public config surface stays narrow.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest concrete history signal for pre-compaction memory flush and nearby memory runtime behavior points to this owner.
